result.summary: Adds an -ipcconnect command-line option to bitcoin-wallet and an -ipcbind option to bitcoin-node in multiprocess builds. When enabled, bitcoin-node listens on a local IPC socket and bitcoin-wallet attempts to connect to it on startup, falling back to offline operation if unavailable.
result.problem: The bitcoin-wallet tool is currently restricted to offline operations and cannot interact with a running node to access chain state, sync balances, or run wallet RPCs.
evidence: PR description: 'The idea is that bitcoin-wallet can be extended in the future to have some online functionality. For example, there could be a bitcoin-wallet sync command that will update balances and sync latest transactions to an unloaded wallet, or a bitcoin-wallet serve subcommand that loads a wallet and serves RPC requests'
Part of the process separation project (issue #28722)
result.scope_notes: This PR sits on top of the multiprocess stack (#10102 and #29409); only the head commit (d8bb996bdf) represents the changes specific to bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect. The rest of the branch carries extensive Cap'n Proto interface bindings and libmultiprocess subtree updates.
result.card: Adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-wallet and -ipcbind to bitcoin-node for multiprocess builds, allowing the wallet utility to connect to a running node process via IPC. Today, bitcoin-wallet is strictly offline and cannot query chain state or sync transactions with an active daemon. The PR establishes the baseline connection mechanism required for proposed online commands such as wallet sync, shell, or RPC serving. It depends on the larger multiprocess branch (#10102 and #29409) and is the base for #19461.
